summary: Stanchieri has a large team of lawyers and a clear structure. The homepage gives a visitor no clear next step and shows no proof, at the moment a client in a stressful situation is choosing a lawyer.

findings.problem: The closing copy says Book a legal consultation, but no scheduling link is provided. Only a Contact Us link appears, and the hero has no action button.
findings.cost: A client who is ready to book has to find a contact page, and many will call the next firm.
findings.fix: A Book a consultation button in the hero and closing section, linked to a calendar.

findings.problem: No testimonials, client outcomes or credentials appear on the homepage, and the 2008 founding date and team size appear only in hidden page data.
findings.cost: Family law clients decide on trust. Without visible proof, they compare on price or call the firm with reviews.
findings.fix: Named reviews, your 2008 history and team size shown near every consultation button.

findings.problem: The lawyer headshot grid repeats the same people several times, and about a dozen images in the services and retainers sections have no image source.
findings.cost: Repeated rows push content down, and missing images leave visible gaps on a page that is meant to look reliable.
findings.fix: One clean team grid and every image in place.

findings.problem: The only listed email is support@stanchierifamilylaw.com, and the page title shows as Home.
findings.cost: A support address looks like customer service, not legal intake, and a page title of Home wastes your search listing.
findings.fix: A dedicated consultation email and a search title that names the firm and city.

redesign: A consultation first homepage with a hero button, a short intake form and a phone number above the fold.
Proof beside every button: named reviews, outcomes and your 2008 history.
Practice area pages written to rank for searches like divorce lawyer Toronto and child custody lawyer Toronto.
